Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Location:
Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

What To Expect

Play an important role in identifying and assessing potential acquisition targets across the P&C value chain, as well as other corporate initiatives, for strategic fit and value generation
Manage the execution of acquisition and divestiture transactions, including but not limited to deal sourcing, due diligence, executive and regulatory approval, transaction documentation, and integration support
Lead the preparation of financial analysis, including building complex models, assessment of synergies / dis-synergies, valuation analysis, and accretion / dilution

Supervise the production of industry benchmarking reports and lead update / development of new industry benchmarking reports - Provide support as required for ad hoc requests from cross-functional teams and other corporate strategic initiatives

What You Bring

Completed university degree, preferably within accounting, business, finance, or actuarial science , with high proven achievement

jobs.description:
About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Our headquarters and most of our team are based in Ottawa. For employees located in Ottawa,

this role follows a hybrid work model, with an expectation of approximately four days per week

in the office at our headquarters. We also welcome remote candidates from anywhere in

Canada.

About The Role

The Vice President, Financial Accounting & Reporting is a senior accounting and controllership executive for a global public company. Working in close partnership with the CFO, the VP, Financial Accounting & Reporting ensures the integrity, discipline, and operational effectiveness of the company’s financial management framework across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, audit oversight, compliance, and revenue accounting globally.

The role serves as a trusted advisor to the CFO and Audit Committee on financial governance, controllership, regulatory readiness, and enterprise risk management related to financial operations and reporting

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

What you will do

Lead the day-to-day operating rhythm of the accounting, external reporting, and internal control functions, with accountability for efficient and accurate close processes, disciplined financial administration, and effective oversight of core accounting operations and global compliance.
Ensure timely, accurate, and decision-useful financial reporting, including external reporting obligations such as OSC and SEC filings and public disclosures, in compliance with IFRS/US GAAP, internal policies, and public-company requirements.
Oversee audit readiness, external audit coordination, control certification support, Canada NI 52-109 requirements, U.S. Sarbanes-Oxley readiness, and the operational processes required to maintain a strong compliance posture across jurisdictions.
Partner with risk management and internal audit.
Support the CFO in Audit Committee matters and serve as a senior operational counterpart on financial governance, controls, and compliance topics.
Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

What we are looking for

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC
reporting, SOX/ICFR, or complex technology clients.
An active CPA designation is required for this role.
Strong presentation and communication skills at the senior management and board level

#VP

#DF-LI1

Work With Impact:
Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Work with Fortune 500 Brands:
Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

Social Responsibility at Kinaxis:
Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Committee weighs in on hiring practices, talent assessment training materials, and mandatory training on unconscious bias and inclusion fundamentals. Sustainability is key to what we do and we’re committed to a long-term net-zero operations strategy. We are involved in our communities and support causes where we can make the most impact.

People matter at Kinaxis and here are some of the perks and benefits we offer, which may vary by location and employee:

Flexible vacation and Kinaxis Days (company-wide days off)
Flexible work options
Physical and mental well-being programs
Regularly scheduled virtual fitness classes
Mentorship programs, training, and career development
Recognition programs and referral rewards
Hackathons

Position Overview:

At Finning, we're committed to delivering exceptional customer outcomes through safe, efficient, and high-performing operations. We are seeking a strategic and visible leader to join our team as Director, Elk Valley Operations, providing enterprise-wide leadership and accountability.

This leadership role will serve as the single point of contact for the site leadership team, driving collaboration across service, parts, supply chain, training, and operational functions to ensure seamless execution and long-term success. With accountability for salaried and hourly employees, this role requires a strong operational leader who can build high-performing teams, develop future leaders, strengthen customer partnerships, and deliver outstanding safety, financial, and operational results. The successful candidate will maintain a strong field presence, spending a minimum of three days per week at mine sites to support employees, customers, and business objectives.

We anticipate the base salary for this position will be between $160,000 - $170,000 yearly. Actual salary will be based on the candidate's experience. This role is also eligible for Regional Wage Allowance and Short Term Incentive Program.

Job Description:

What You'll Do

Provide strategic and operational leadership for Finning's Elk Valley operations, ensuring alignment across service, parts, supply chain, training, and support functions to achieve business objectives.
Act as the primary relationship owner and trusted advisor for the customer site leadership team, driving operational excellence and contract execution.
Champion a culture of safety excellence by leading health and safety initiatives, ensuring compliance with all regulatory and company requirements, and fostering an incident-free workplace.
Lead, coach, and develop leaders across the region while building a strong succession pipeline and creating opportunities for employee growth and career development.
Oversee regional financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, contract management, asset optimization, and delivery of revenue and profitability targets.
Drive continuous improvement through the review of key operational metrics related to safety, quality, customer experience, productivity, and cost management.
Partner with labour relations stakeholders to build and maintain positive relationships with unionized employees and union representatives.
Maintain a strong and visible presence at mine sites, strengthening customer relationships, supporting employees, and ensuring operational excellence across the region.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of progressive leadership experience within mining, heavy equipment, industrial, or related operational environments, including experience leading leaders.
Demonstrated success managing large-scale operations with accountability for safety, financial performance, workforce planning, and customer outcomes.
Strong operational knowledge across service, parts, supply chain, maintenance, and support functions, with the ability to lead cross-functional teams toward common goals.
Proven experience managing customer contracts, executing operational commitments, and building trusted relationships with key stakeholders.
Exceptional leadership, coaching, and talent development capabilities with a track record of building engaged, high-performing teams.
Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, performance management, and strategic planning.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.
Previous mining industry experience and knowledge of heavy equipment operations, safety management systems, labour relations, and operational best practices are considered strong assets.

What Does Finning Offer?

Comprehensive pension program with employer contributions
Employee Share Purchase Plan with company matching
Employer paid extended health, dental, and medical benefits available from day 1
This role is eligible for Finning’s Short Term Incentive Program
Competitive total rewards package designed to support your financial, physical, and personal well-being

Description

At Xe, we live currencies
. Founded in 1993, Xe is a global leader in currency exchange and international money transfers. What began as a simple currency converter has grown into a platform trusted by over 300 million people each year. We provide a comprehensive range of currency services and products, including our real-time exchange rates, Currency Converter, Market Analysis and Currency Data API, supporting 130+ currencies across 190+ countries with quick, easy, secure Money Transfers for individuals and businesses. We leverage technology to deliver these services through our website, mobile app, and by phone. Backed by Euronet, we process more than $115 billion in global payments annually. Xe is profitable, product-led, and focused on building reliable, user-first tools that make moving money across borders easier for everyone.

Our Principles

At Xe, we value people who take initiative, think big, and follow through. We’re curious by nature and not afraid to ask what if or try something new. Everyone’s voice matters here. We expect people to speak up, bring ideas, and take ownership of their work. We don’t micromanage. We trust each other to make good calls, take responsibility, and move fast when it counts. And we care about community. Not in a vague corporate way, but in the sense that we have each other’s backs, stay open to feedback, and build a culture of trust and real collaboration.

Ambition. We dream big, try things out, and always ask “why not?” and “what if?” We’re ambitious in our thinking and our delivery.
Responsibility. We get involved, bring our perspective, and are always open to new ideas. We take personal responsibility.
Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

The Role.
The Head of Consumer is the senior owner of Xe’s Consumer business in the United States and Canada, accountable for its strategy, proposition and commercial performance. Product, Marketing and Growth sit in global teams, so you will lead through influence: aligning them, along with Pricing, Sales, Customer Success, Care and Operations, behind the North America plan.

Responsibilities

This is a builder’s role. You will run the NAM Consumer business like a founder, owning revenue, profitability, acquisition, activation, retention, wallet share and customer lifetime value — and opening new channels to reach more customers. The role suits a digitally fluent leader with a background across product, marketing and growth in a fast-paced startup or scale-up. You know what great looks like in each function and can push global teams to deliver it for North American customers. Responsibilities include:

Consumer Strategy & Commercial Performance

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.
Own end-to-end commercial performance across the customer lifecycle: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, wallet share and lifetime value.
Define the priorities, targets and operating rhythm for the Consumer business, and align regional and global stakeholders behind them.
Track a fast-moving competitive set — digital money transfer apps, neobanks, big tech wallets and incumbent banks — and spot new pockets of growth, such as high-value corridors and underserved diaspora communities.

Channel Expansion

Identify, build and scale new acquisition and distribution channels for Consumer in the US and Canada — for example, affiliate and referral programs, embedded and B2B2C distribution, community, diaspora and employer channels, and marketplaces.
Build the business case for each channel, run pilots, and scale those that hit CAC, volume and margin targets.
Lead commercial discussions with channel partners, including RFPs, and manage those relationships for ongoing performance.
Work with Compliance and Operations so each new channel launches safely and integrates cleanly into the customer journey.

Influencing Product, Marketing, Growth & Pricing

Be the voice of the NAM consumer with global Product, Marketing and Growth teams: bring market insight, set regional priorities, and secure roadmap and investment commitments.
Develop and own Customer Value Propositions for each Consumer segment in the US and Canada, and brief global teams on the features, benefits, pricing and service levels each segment needs.
Own regional go-to-market and in-market delivery of new products and propositions, coordinating cross-functional teams to maximize uptake and commercial return.
Champion test-and-learn on NAM funnels, onboarding and messaging, and hold partner teams to agreed outcomes.
Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Performance Management & Reporting

Build and run a Consumer performance framework covering acquisition, conversion, activation, transactions, active customers, retention cohorts, revenue, profitability, CAC, LTV, channel performance, customer experience and product adoption.
Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.
Use data, customer insight and commercial analysis to guide investment decisions and close performance gaps.

How Success is Measured.
Success in the role will be measured through a combination of commercial, customer and operational outcomes, including:

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.
Growth in active Consumer customers and transaction volumes.
Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.
Improved acquisition, conversion and activation, from sign-up to first transfer.
Increased retention, repeat usage and wallet share.
Adoption and commercial performance of new products and propositions in NAM.
Improved customer experience and service performance (e.g. NPS, app ratings, SLAs).
Stronger cross-functional execution and delivery of NAM priorities by global teams.

What You Bring

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.
Hands-on leadership experience across Product, Marketing and Growth — ideally having owned or run more than one of these functions.
A track record in a high-growth, fast-paced startup or scale-up environment, ideally in consumer fintech, payments, money transfer, neobanking or another digital consumer business.
Proven results scaling a consumer product: driving acquisition, activation, retention and monetization with measurable impact.
Fluency with the modern growth stack — product analytics, experimentation platforms, CRM and lifecycle tools, attribution and paid acquisition channels.
Strong commercial and analytical skills, with a firm grasp of unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) and data-driven decision-making.
Experience building and leading high-performing, cross-functional teams, and comfort influencing in a matrixed global organization.
A bias for action: you move fast, ship, learn and iterate, while keeping the bigger strategic picture in view.
Excellent communication and storytelling, from team stand-ups to senior leadership.
Understanding of, or a strong appetite to learn, regulated financial services in the US and Canada.
Deep customer empathy and familiarity with US and Canadian consumer markets.

Perks & Benefits (Canada)

Competitive salary and incentive.
Vacation+ personal days + day off for your birthday + sick time + holidays
Volunteering day for a charity of your choice
Healthcare
Life & Disability insurance
Plumm Mental Health and Wellbeing
Matched employer RRSP contribution (subject to limits)
Discounted Euronet Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP)
A chance to grow your career in a mission-driven global company.

Why Join Us?
You'll be part of a fast-moving team where your contributions directly impact growth. We invest in our people with tools, mentorship, and opportunities to level up fast-whether that's moving into closing roles or leadership paths. You'll also play a key role in shaping how we go to market in the competitive payments space, using real insights and industry benchmarks to stay ahead of the curve. Provide strategic and operational leadership for Finning's Elk Valley operations, ensuring alignment across service, parts, supply chain, training, and support functions to achieve business objectives.

Maintain a strong and visible presence at mine sites, strengthening customer relationships, supporting employees, and ensuring operational excellence across the region.

Demonstrated success managing large-scale operations with accountability for safety, financial performance, workforce planning, and customer outcomes.
Strong operational knowledge across service, parts, supply chain, maintenance, and support functions, with the ability to lead cross-functional teams toward common goals.
Proven experience managing customer contracts, executing operational commitments, and building trusted relationships with key stakeholders.
Exceptional leadership, coaching, and talent development capabilities with a track record of building engaged, high-performing teams.
Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, performance management, and strategic planning.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.
Previous mining industry experience and knowledge of heavy equipment operations, safety management systems, labour relations, and operational best practices are considered strong assets.

Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

Results orientation and a bias for action

Associate Directors lead the day-to-day delivery of engagements and work closely with senior professionals and testifying experts on complex issues at the intersection of valuation, finance, accounting, economics and law. About GHD | Energy Business

GHD’s Energy business is positioned for significant growth across the Americas, with priority areas including power generation, transmission and distribution, battery energy storage systems, hydropower, future fuels, gas-to-power, renewable natural gas, carbon capture, and major project delivery for mining and industrial clients. We bring together advisory, engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project management, and delivery expertise to support clients across the full project lifecycle.

Our Hybrid Model:
Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect, and excel in our vibrant environment.

Location:
Ontario (Waterloo, Toronto, Mississauga, Markham, Whitby, Peterborough, St. Catherines)

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking an experienced Nuclear Project Director to support the growth and delivery of complex nuclear and energy capital projects across Canada and North America. This role will provide senior leadership across strategic project portfolios, major project execution, client engagement, governance, risk management, and multidisciplinary delivery. The successful candidate will bring a proven ability to lead large capital programs from proposal, early planning through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

This is a senior, delivery and client-facing leadership role for a professional who can quickly assess business priorities, establish project discipline, build strong delivery teams, and support clients through complex decisions involving capital allocation, operational risk, reliability, safety, stakeholder expectations, and long-term asset performance.

Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position will see you involved in:

Serve as Project Director on complex nuclear, energy, and major infrastructure and advisory projects, providing senior oversight from concept and feasibility through execution, commissioning, and closeout.
Lead strategic project portfolios, including capital planning, project selection, governance, prioritization, and execution readiness for clients with large-scale CAPEX programs.
Support GHD’s Energy growth objectives by helping originate, shape, and deliver opportunities across nuclear power, nuclear waste, nuclear decommissioning, renewable power generation, hydropower, transmission and distribution, and industrial energy systems.
Partner with Market and Sector Leaders, Business Group Leaders, Relationship Managers, technical specialists, and regional delivery teams to develop capture plans, position GHD for strategic pursuits, and convert opportunities into profitable backlog.
Provide executive-level client leadership, building trusted relationships with nuclear operators, OEMs, waste management, Indigenous communities, government agencies, contraction partners, and financing organizations.
Lead multidisciplinary project teams, including engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project controls, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and operations readiness resources.
Establish and implement project governance, risk management, change management, commercial controls, communication protocols, and decision-making frameworks that improve delivery certainty.
Drive safety leadership and promote a strong site safety culture across project teams, contractors, and client stakeholders.
Guide value engineering, constructability reviews, scope control, cost optimization, schedule recovery, and issue resolution on major capital projects.
Mentor project managers and emerging leaders, strengthening GHD’s project delivery capability and helping build a scalable major projects platform across Energy.
Collaborate across Canada, the United States, and global GHD networks to leverage technical capability, Global Collaboration Centres, and best-practice delivery models.

What you will bring to the team:

Engineering degree or related technical qualification is preferred; graduate education in project management, business administration, or a related discipline is an asset.
Professional licensure or eligibility preferred (P.Eng. + PMP).
15-18 years of experience in the nuclear, energy, or related sector, including business development, project management, and technical leadership for major infrastructure.
Extensive senior leadership experience in project direction, project portfolio management, capital project execution, operations leadership, and general management within energy, nuclear, aerospace, or related sectors.
Demonstrated experience leading major capital projects and portfolios, including projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Proven ability to lead end-to-end project execution, including facility design, equipment selection, consultant and contractor selection, construction management, commissioning, and operations turnover.
Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing scope, cost, schedule, procurement, contracts, risk, change, and governance on complex projects.
Track record of improving project outcomes through value engineering, contractor engagement, cost optimization, project controls, and disciplined issue resolution.
Experience supporting nuclear or energy sector clients through strategic growth, operational improvement, reliability, maintenance, and asset performance initiatives.
Strong executive presence and ability to work effectively with senior leadership teams, Boards of Directors, clients, contractors, government stakeholders, and community partners.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and an understanding of the importance of respectful engagement, partnership, social license, and community benefit in major project development.
Ability to build, motivate, and lead high-performing teams over multi-year project lifecycles.
Proven experience in nuclear business development in a market-facing role is required.
Commitment to health, safety, quality, inclusion, collaboration, and GHD’s values as an employee-owned organization.
Experience with Design Bid Build (DBB), Design Build (DB), and alternative delivery projects such as Progressive DB, Integrated Project Delivery/Alliance and/or P3 considered an asset.
